name: Agentic Tool Use in Large Language Models (Hu et al.)
venue: arXiv preprint (arXiv:2604.00835, cs.CL). Submitted 1 Apr 2026 (v1). Not a peer-reviewed venue; arXiv-issued DOI 10.48550/arXiv.2604.00835. (Verified from the arXiv abstract page; submission history shows [v1] Wed, 1 Apr 2026, 976 KB.)
authors_affiliation: Jinchao Hu (School of Computer Science and Technology, Harbin Institute of Technology, Shenzhen, China); Meizhi Zhong (TikTok Inc, Beijing, China); Kehai Chen (HIT Shenzhen, China; corresponding-style senior author); Xuefeng Bai (HIT Shenzhen, China); Min Zhang (HIT Shenzhen, China). code_url: N/A (survey; no official code/implementation or paper-list repository is announced in the abstract page or paper. The many citations to GitHub-hosted frameworks such as ReAct, ToolLLM, Search-R1, VerlTool, OpenAI Swarm, AgentKit are third-party works, not artifacts of this survey.)
maintained_repo_url: N/A (no continuously-updated authors' paper list or leaderboard is associated with this survey; it is a frozen v1 arXiv PDF/HTML as of indexing.)
task_domain: Survey / taxonomy of agentic tool use (function calling) in LLMs. Spans tool-use across QA/knowledge retrieval, mathematical and program-aided reasoning, code/software engineering, web and computer/GUI agents, embodied/robotic action, and safety. Tool use is framed as the mechanism that operationalizes action for LLM agents (search, computation, external system control).
problem_setting: This is an analytical literature survey, not a method or system with original experiments. It organizes the agentic-tool-use literature into three methodological paradigms distinguished by their optimization signal: (I) Prompting as Plug-and-Play (frozen weights, in-context control), (II) Supervised Tool Learning (SFT on labeled/synthetic tool-use data), and (III) Reward-Driven Tool Policy Learning (RL over multi-turn tool interaction). It treats evaluation as a cross-cutting fourth dimension. Settings covered range from offline single-call function calling to interactive, stateful, multi-turn single-agent and multi-agent deployments; supervision availability is precisely the organizing axis (none/in-context -> supervised -> reward). The survey itself defines no controlled experimental protocol, training run, or benchmark of its own; it offers a six-dimension comparison of prior surveys (chronological evolution, paradigm taxonomy, tool coverage, training data, evaluation landscape, open challenges) and qualitative benchmark tables.
what_is_retrieved: N/A as an artifact (the survey itself retrieves nothing). As surveyed content: tools/APIs and tool documentation (the central retrieved object, e.g., AnyTool hierarchical API retrieval, Gorilla retrieval over evolving API docs); reasoning-action programs/templates from external task libraries (ART); search/web evidence and knowledge documents (WebGPT, Search-R1, HotpotQA-style retrieval); and reusable synthesized tools/skills from an evolving tool library (TroVE, LATM). The survey's evaluation section devotes an explicit category to 'Tool Retrieval and Selection.'
retrieval_grounding: Survey-level: covers BOTH access to STATIC/dynamic external tool corpora (curated function pools, large real-world API collections such as ToolLLM's 16000+ APIs, evolving API documentation in Gorilla, MCP-served tool marketplaces) and GROWING agent-curated stores (TroVE/LATM tool libraries, Titans test-time long-term memory). HYBRID overall; the survey itself is grounded in no single corpus.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: N/A (survey; defines no retrieval objective of its own). Surveyed tool-retrieval work spans top-k selection from large candidate pools (StableToolBench, API-Bank), hierarchical narrowing of the candidate space before invocation (AnyTool), and whether-or-not / when-to-call decisions (When2Call, WTU-Eval) that emphasize precision-driven necessity rather than fixed top-k. No completeness metric is standardized.
cbr_cycle_coverage: N/A (the survey is not a case-based reasoning system and implements no Retrieve/Reuse/Revise/Retain cycle; CBR is not an organizing concept of this survey).
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The survey does not frame agentic tool use as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner; it organizes the field around the optimization signal (in-context control, supervised signals, reward feedback).
retrieval_unit: N/A (survey defines no single retrieval unit). Surveyed units: tool-API / function signature (the dominant unit, with its docstring/specification), reasoning-action program or template (ART task library), retrieved document/passage or web snippet (search-augmented QA, Search-R1), and reusable synthesized tool/program (TroVE, LATM). At evaluation time the relevant unit is the candidate function plus its specification.
index_source: N/A for the survey. Surveyed Agentic tool-use systems draw on static curated function pools and large real-world API collections (ToolLLM, StableToolBench), live/evolving API documentation (Gorilla; the future MCP-served dynamic tool marketplaces), and growing agent-curated tool libraries (TroVE continuous tool-library evolution; LATM tool making). The survey builds no index itself.
index_structure_topology: N/A (survey has no index of its own). It reviews multiple organizations: flat candidate function pools (BFCL, ToolEyes), HIERARCHICAL retrieval over large API libraries (AnyTool's hierarchical agents narrowing the candidate space; ToolLLM's depth-first/tree-style API exploration), dependency-aware computation graphs over tool calls (LLMCompiler organizes tool calls as a dependency-aware graph for parallel execution), and protocol-served dynamic tool catalogs (envisioned MCP marketplaces).
retriever_type: N/A (survey; no retriever implemented). Surveyed retrievers include dense/embedding-based tool retrieval over documentation (Gorilla retrieval), hierarchical LLM-agent-driven retrieval (AnyTool), and search-engine/web APIs as retrievers in RL-trained settings (Search-R1, DeepResearcher). The LLM frequently acts as router/selector over candidate tools rather than as the retriever.
retriever_learning_signal: N/A (survey; trains no retriever). It reviews the spectrum it explicitly champions: from in-context/prompted tool selection (no retriever training; Paradigm I) to supervised/API-aware fine-tuning for accurate selection and calling (Gorilla combines retrieval with API-aware fine-tuning; NexusRaven; APIGen), to reward-driven policies that learn when and which tool to call from environmental feedback (ReTool, ToolRL, Search-R1). The survey itself proposes no learning signal.
query_construction: N/A (survey). Surveyed query/key construction includes raw task instruction matched against tool docstrings (function-calling benchmarks), decomposed sub-questions (Self-Ask, Least-to-Most), thought-conditioned reasoning steps that decide the next action (ReAct), and explicit plans whose subtasks are dispatched to tools (ReWOO planner-worker, LLMCompiler). The survey prescribes no single construction method.
query_granularity: N/A (survey). Surveyed systems range from task-level one-shot tool selection (decoupled planning, ReWOO/HuggingGPT plan-then-execute), to step/state-level per-turn action selection (ReAct interleaved loop, RL multi-turn policies). The survey commits to no single granularity, instead organizing by control flow (interleaved vs decoupled vs program-aided).
when_to_retrieve: N/A (survey). Surveyed control spans one-shot/plan-then-execute (ReWOO, HuggingGPT, LLMCompiler), iterative per-step interleaving (ReAct, Reflexion, LATS tree search), and learned/adaptive decisions about whether to invoke a tool at all (ReTool RL distinguishes tool-needed vs internal-knowledge cases; When2Call/WTU-Eval evaluate this decision boundary).
retrieval_trigger_signal: N/A (survey defines no single trigger). Surveyed triggers: the model's own thought/decision in the Thought-Action-Observation loop (ReAct), verbal self-reflection on failure (Reflexion), external-tool-grounded verification (CRITIC, Chain-of-Verification), tree-search expansion (LATS), and learned RL policies that decide when a tool is necessary (ReTool). Evaluation benchmarks When2Call and WTU-Eval target the whether-or-not-to-call signal explicitly.
reranking: N/A (survey; no reranking stage of its own). Reranking/selection over large tool pools is reviewed implicitly via hierarchical candidate narrowing (AnyTool) and tool-selection benchmarks (StableToolBench, API-Bank), but the survey contributes no reranking method.
retrieved_context_refinement: N/A (survey). It reviews refinement operations in surveyed systems: self-reflection/self-refinement over trajectories (Reflexion, Self-Refine), tool-grounded verification and critique (CRITIC, Chain-of-Verification), and System-2-Attention-style context regeneration plus TroVE tool-library curation flagged as future directions. The survey implements no refinement pipeline.
tool_document_engineering: N/A as a contribution (survey). It discusses that accurate tool use depends on understanding tool specifications/docstrings, that Gorilla uses up-to-date documentation at inference time (retrieval + API-aware fine-tuning), that NexusRaven emphasizes zero-shot function calling from tool descriptions, and that APIGen produces verifiable synthetic function-calling data; it proposes no new tool-document-indexing technique itself.
index_content_separation: N/A (survey; no index-vs-content separation mechanism of its own). It notes hierarchical retrieval that narrows a large candidate space before loading/invoking specific tools (AnyTool) and the envisioned MCP model where a lightweight protocol-served catalog is queried before binding a tool, but these are reviewed, not contributed.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A as a contribution, but a central FUTURE-DIRECTION theme. The survey's first future direction is 'Standardization and the MCP Revolution': the Model Context Protocol (Hou et al., 2025) as a standardized interface decoupling agents from tool implementations, turning integration from quadratic to linear complexity, and enabling dynamic, protocol-compliant tool marketplaces that agents query and subscribe to in real time. It also reviews RESTful API interaction (RestGPT) and large real-world API ecosystems (ToolLLM, Gorilla). The survey itself maintains no live tool index.
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A as a contribution (survey). It reviews dependency modeling in surveyed systems: LLMCompiler organizes tool calls as a dependency-aware computation graph enabling parallel execution of independent subtasks, ReWOO's planner emits subtasks with variable assignments passed between steps, and NESTFUL evaluates nested API calls where one call's output feeds the next. The survey contributes no dependency-graph retrieval formalism of its own.
how_retrieved_used: N/A as a method. The survey describes how surveyed systems use tools/retrieved content: prompt/context augmentation and in-context interaction in Paradigm I; internalization into model weights via SFT in Paradigm II (teaching tool-call syntax and logic); and reward-driven policy optimization in Paradigm III where tool-call outcomes provide training signal. Code/program execution is used as an externalized computation backend (PAL, PoT) and as an action space (CodeAct, Code as Policies).
planning_integration: N/A as a method. The survey explicitly organizes Paradigm I by how reasoning/planning interfaces with tool execution: (a) Interleaved Reasoning and Action (per-step thought-action-observation loops; ReAct, Reflexion, CRITIC, LATS tree search); (b) Decoupled Planning and Execution (plan-then-execute; ReWOO planner-worker, LLMCompiler dependency graph + parallel calls, AdaPlanner feedback-revised plans, HuggingGPT/TaskMatrix.AI central planner over experts); and (c) Program-Aided Reasoning (code as the planning/execution medium; PAL, PoT, ViperGPT, Code as Policies, LATM/CREATOR tool creation). Paradigm III integrates planning into RL over multi-turn rollouts (Search-R1, SimpleTIR end-to-end).
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: N/A (survey). It contrasts per-step interleaving (per thought-action-observation cycle in ReAct/Reflexion), plan-level / per-answer decoupling (ReWOO, LLMCompiler issuing batched/parallel calls), and per-tool-call-within-a-rollout interleaving in RL multi-turn tool-integrated reasoning (SimpleTIR, Search-R1, ReTool). The survey reviews these styles rather than fixing one granularity.
adaptation_mechanism: N/A (not a CBR method; the survey contributes no retrieved-case adaptation mechanism). Adjacent surveyed mechanisms include verbal-reflection-driven revision (Reflexion), execution-feedback-driven plan revision (AdaPlanner, TRICE execution feedback, Retroformer retrospective policy gradient).
retrieved_item_representation: N/A (survey). Surveyed surface forms injected/used: free-text tool documentation and function schemas (function calling), executable code/programs (PAL, PoT, CodeAct, TroVE/LATM synthesized tools), reasoning-action programs/templates (ART), and natural-language reasoning traces interleaved with tool outputs (ReAct trajectories). The survey injects nothing itself.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: N/A (survey). Surveyed units range from a single concrete tool/API call and its arguments, to reusable procedural skills/programs (LATM, TroVE, CREATOR tool creation), to higher-level reasoning-action templates retrieved from a task library (ART). The survey reviews this spectrum rather than fixing an abstraction level.
noise_robustness_mechanism: N/A (survey contributes none of its own). It reviews robustness mechanisms in surveyed systems: self-reflection and iterative refinement (Reflexion, Self-Refine), external-tool-grounded verification/critique (CRITIC, Chain-of-Verification), and a dedicated Safety-and-Reliability evaluation layer covering indirect prompt injection (ToolSword, InjecAgent), sandboxed risk emulation (ToolEmu), and risk-awareness judgment (R-Judge, SafetyBench, PsySafe). Future directions add NeMo Guardrails and PromptArmor as defenses.
memory_type: N/A as an artifact. Surveyed memory spans episodic/long-context memory (Generative Agents, MemGPT memory management), skill/tool libraries (Voyager skill acquisition, TroVE/LATM tool libraries), and test-time neural long-term memory (Titans, flagged as a future direction). The survey treats memory as part of the agentic architecture (reasoning core + planning + memory + action) rather than implementing one.
write_back: N/A as a method. Surveyed systems DO write back: Voyager stores acquired skills, TroVE continuously evolves an agent's tool library, LATM creates and stores reusable tools, MemGPT manages long-context memory, and Titans memorizes historical context at test time. The survey itself stores nothing.
online_growth: N/A as a method. Surveyed agent stores grow online/at test time (TroVE continuous tool-library evolution; Titans test-time memorization; Voyager incremental skill acquisition), and the survey's 'Agentic Self-Consistency and Continuous Evolution' future direction foresees agents curating their own internal libraries of synthesized tools and usage patterns instead of resetting after each session. The survey itself has no growing store.
write_back_trigger: N/A (survey; no write-back trigger of its own). Surveyed triggers include reflective writes after self-critique (Reflexion), on-success skill/tool acquisition (Voyager, TroVE, LATM creating verified reusable tools), and test-time memorization of salient context (Titans). The survey discusses continuous self-extension as a future goal without standardizing a trigger.
failure_experience_usage: N/A (survey). It highlights learning from failed executions as a key challenge and reviews several approaches: Reflexion's verbal self-reflection over failed trajectories reused in later attempts, Retroformer's retrospective learning over past tool-use trajectories, and TRICE's credit assignment that strengthens steps contributing to correct answers while suppressing noisy/unhelpful actions. The survey contributes no failure-storage scheme of its own.
memory_evolution_update: N/A (survey). It frames continuous tool-library curation and self-evolution (TroVE, agents curating internal libraries) and test-time memory updates (Titans) as future directions, but proposes no single post-write update policy (append/merge/refine/prune).
retrieval_as_learned_policy: N/A (survey). Paradigm III explicitly covers tool use as a learned/RL-optimized policy: ReTool learns when external tools are needed vs internal knowledge, ToolRL treats reward as central to tool learning, Search-R1 trains the reasoning-retrieval interaction via RL, and SimpleTIR unifies reasoning and tool execution in one end-to-end RL loop. The survey reviews (does not implement) retrieval/tool-selection-as-learned-policy and identifies multi-tool credit assignment in long tool chains as a core open problem.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: N/A as a method. Surveyed and future-direction theme: multi-agent orchestration and standardized interoperability are highlighted (OpenAI Swarm lightweight handoffs between specialized agents, AgentKit structured reasoning with dynamic graphs, MetaGPT/AutoGen/OpenDevin multi-agent collaboration), and MCP is positioned as enabling a tool built once to be usable by any compliant agent/framework (cross-framework sharing). The survey reviews rather than implements cross-agent/cross-framework sharing.
benchmarks: N/A as original experiments (survey reports no results of its own). It catalogs benchmarks across three evaluation levels. Tool Usage Correctness: BFCL (Berkeley Function Calling Leaderboard), ToolEyes, T-Eval, API-Bank, StableToolBench, Gorilla, When2Call, WTU-Eval, NexusRaven, NESTFUL. Task Completion: AIME(25), MATH/MATH-500, GSM8K, TabMWP, FreshQA, ToolQA, HotpotQA, 2WikiMultihopQA, Natural Questions, TriviaQA, MMLU, StrategyQA, HumanEval, MBPP, BigCodeBench, SWE-bench, BIRD, Spider 2.0, DSBench, DS-1000, InterCode, SheetBench/SpreadsheetBench, FinQA, SciBench, SciCode, BioPlanner, ChemCrow, MedAgent-Bench. Tool-Driven Interaction: WebArena, VisualWebArena, WebVoyager, Mind2Web, GAIA, TravelPlanner, WorldSense, OSWorld, OS-Copilot, OmniACT, AndroidWorld, AppWorld, AppAgent, ScreenAgent, GUI-World, OfficeBench, WorkArena, tau-bench, TheAgentCompany, CodeAct; plus Safety: ToolSword, InjecAgent, ToolEmu, SafetyBench, R-Judge, PsySafe.
benchmark_family: Survey-level grouping into three evolving levels: (1) Tool Usage Correctness -- function-call validity (BFCL/ToolEyes/T-Eval), tool retrieval and selection (API-Bank/StableToolBench/Gorilla), tool-use decisions (When2Call/WTU-Eval), compositional invocation (NexusRaven/NESTFUL); (2) Task Completion -- math/knowledge QA (GSM8K, MATH, AIME, HotpotQA, ToolQA, FreshQA), programming/data (HumanEval, MBPP, BigCodeBench, SWE-bench, BIRD/Spider 2.0, DSBench, InterCode), scientific/professional (SciBench, SciCode, BioPlanner, ChemCrow, MedAgent-Bench); (3) Tool-Driven Interaction -- web (WebArena/VisualWebArena/WebVoyager/Mind2Web/GAIA), computer/GUI/OS and mobile (OSWorld/OmniACT/AndroidWorld/AppWorld), workplace (OfficeBench/WorkArena/tau-bench/TheAgentCompany), and safety/reliability (ToolSword/InjecAgent/ToolEmu/R-Judge/SafetyBench/PsySafe). Maps onto the collection families: tool (ToolBench/API-Bank/BFCL), web (Mind2Web/WebArena), code (SWE-bench), QA/multi-hop (HotpotQA).
baselines: N/A (survey; runs no head-to-head experiments and reports no baselines of its own). Its comparative analysis is qualitative: a Table-1 comparison of representative prior surveys (Zhao et al. 2023; Wang et al. 2024; Mialon et al. 2023; Qu et al. 2025; Shen 2024; Chen et al. 2025) along six dimensions, showing only 'Ours' covers all six (chronological evolution + paradigm taxonomy + tool coverage + training data + evaluation landscape + open challenges); and a paradigm-vs-paradigm contrast (Prompting vs Supervised vs Reward-Driven) by strengths and failure modes.
key_metrics: N/A (survey; reports no quantitative metrics of its own). It catalogs the evaluation signals used across levels: function-call validity / schema-constrained correctness and fine-grained error diagnosis (BFCL, ToolEyes, T-Eval), tool retrieval/selection accuracy, whether-or-not / when-to-call decision accuracy (When2Call, WTU-Eval), end-to-end task success / pass rate (math accuracy, code pass@k, QA accuracy, SWE-bench resolved rate), interactive task-success and trajectory match (WebArena task success, Mind2Web trajectory match, tau-bench state outcome / policy compliance), and safety/attack-resistance and risk-judgment signals (ToolSword, InjecAgent, R-Judge).
headline_result: N/A (survey; no headline number). Its central contribution is conceptual: a unified three-paradigm evolutionary taxonomy of agentic tool use -- (I) Prompting as Plug-and-Play, (II) Supervised Tool Learning, (III) Reward-Driven Tool Policy Learning -- distinguished by optimization signal (in-context control / supervised signals / reward feedback), plus a cross-cutting three-level evaluation landscape (tool usage correctness -> task completion -> tool-driven interaction). It argues the three paradigms are complementary and that production-grade systems will likely combine all three.
ablations: N/A (survey; conducts no experiments and reports no component ablations). Its closest analogue is the qualitative per-paradigm strengths/failure-mode analysis: Prompting is flexible, interpretable, low deployment cost but suffers high latency/token cost and brittleness on complex multi-step tasks; Supervised internalizes tool-use behavior into weights (efficiency/reliability) but is bottlenecked by large-scale high-quality data construction and risks degrading generalist ability (motivating AgentTuning/Lemur balance); Reward-driven enables exploration, error recovery, and long-horizon adaptation but faces multi-tool credit assignment over long tool-call chains.
evaluation_decoupling: N/A as original measurement (survey performs no evaluation). It explicitly DECOUPLES diagnostic intrinsic correctness (function-call validity, tool retrieval/selection, fine-grained error diagnosis via ToolEyes/T-Eval) from end-to-end task-completion success and from interactive task success/state outcomes, treating these as three distinct, progressively higher evaluation levels.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Survey-level: it argues evaluation must capture both. It highlights step-wise/process-oriented diagnostic benchmarks (T-Eval decomposing tool use into intermediate steps; ToolEyes separating intent-understanding, format-alignment, and tool-selection errors) alongside end-to-end outcome benchmarks (task success), and notes interaction-level evaluation must also assess process properties like error recovery, policy compliance (tau-bench), and safety, not only final outcomes.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: N/A as original measurement (no cost numbers of its own). It discusses efficiency/cost qualitatively as a primary axis: Prompting incurs high latency and token overhead from repeated prompting; decoupled planning (ReWOO) and parallel function calling (LLMCompiler) reduce interaction overhead; Supervised learning internalizes tool use to cut prompting cost; Reward-driven methods (ReTool) reduce unnecessary tool calls; and the MCP future direction reframes integration cost from quadratic to linear complexity.
context_budget_and_selection_count: N/A (survey; no token budget or k of its own). It reviews mechanisms that manage budget/selection in surveyed systems -- hierarchical retrieval narrowing a large candidate tool space before invocation (AnyTool), long-context memory management (MemGPT), and UI-guided visual token selection for high-resolution screens (ShowUI, future direction) -- but prescribes no fixed-k or token budget.
survey_scope_and_axes: Primary organizing axis: an explicitly EVOLUTIONARY three-paradigm taxonomy by optimization signal -- (I) Prompting as Plug-and-Play (Sec.3: Interleaved Reasoning and Action; Decoupled Planning and Execution; Program-Aided Reasoning), (II) Supervised Tool Learning (Sec.4: Self-Supervised Data Generation; Large-Scale Instruction Tuning; Process-Oriented and Alignment-Focused Tuning), (III) Reward-Driven Tool Policy Learning (Sec.5: Strategic Decision Optimization; End-to-End Policy Learning for Multi-Turn Reasoning; Holistic and Multimodal Agentic Frameworks) -- plus a developmental timeline (Sec.2: early concept formation -> prompt-driven agency 2022-2023 -> supervised tool learning 2023-2024 -> policy for autonomous optimization 2024-present), a cross-cutting three-level evaluation taxonomy (Sec.6: tool usage correctness / task completion / tool-driven interaction), and five future directions (Sec.7: MCP standardization; multimodal/embodied agentic foundation models; agentic self-consistency and continuous evolution; higher safety/trustworthiness; human-agent symbiosis and workflow reshaping). Reference/coverage window roughly 2017-2026; reference count [uncertain] (the paper has an extensive bibliography of ~200+ entries based on in-text citation indices up to ~bib.bib210, but the exact final count is not stated in the abstract).
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (this is a survey, not a benchmark; it constructs no dataset of its own). It does annotate cataloged benchmarks by attributes in its tables (Year, Primary Focus, Executable, Compositional, Tool Source for correctness benchmarks; Task Type, Tool Role, Executable, Open-Ended for task-completion; Trajectory, Target, Challenge, Signal for interaction), e.g., ToolLLM is described as covering 16000+ real-world APIs and ToolAlpaca as 3000 simulated cases (in Sec.2 prose).
builds_on: Builds on and synthesizes the agentic-LLM and tool-learning literature it reviews: prompting foundations (Chain-of-Thought, ReAct, Reflexion, Tree of Thoughts; PAL/PoT program-aided reasoning), supervised tool learning (TALM, WebCPM, Toolformer, ToolAlpaca, ToolLLM, Gorilla, APIGen, FireAct, AgentTuning, Lemur), and reward-driven policy learning (ReTool, Retroformer, TRICE, Search-R1, SimpleTIR, RLFactory, VerlTool). It positions itself relative to prior surveys it tabulates: Zhao et al. (2023) and Wang et al. (2024a) agent-architecture surveys, Mialon et al. (2023) augmented-LM survey, Qu et al. (2025) tool-learning survey, Shen (2024), and Chen et al. (2025b).
contrasts_with: Explicitly contrasts itself with prior surveys (Table 1) that provide a largely static snapshot and lack a methodological-evolution view: Zhao et al. (2023), Wang et al. (2024a), Mialon et al. (2023) emphasize agent architecture but no paradigm taxonomy/tool coverage/training-data axis; Qu et al. (2025), Shen (2024), Chen et al. (2025b) cover taxonomy/tool/data but (variously) lack the chronological-evolution axis or evaluation landscape. The survey's distinguishing claim is the evolutionary three-paradigm synthesis (in-context -> supervised -> reward) with evaluation as a co-evolving cross-cutting dimension. It also internally contrasts the three paradigms against one another by strengths and failure modes.
lineage: Surveys group. A 2026 evolutionary survey of agentic tool use / function calling that organizes the field by optimization signal (prompting -> supervised tool learning -> reward-driven tool policy learning) and adds a tool-retrieval/selection evaluation category. It serves as an umbrella reference linking the tool-use sub-topics in this collection -- tool retrieval/selection (relevant to Group D tool-retrieval works such as ToolLLM, Gorilla, AnyTool, ToolRet) and reward-driven/agentic-RL methods -- rather than being a method within any single sub-topic.
